description: tests/build_first_valid_path.rs covers: positive (tc60), NoValidPath (AlwaysRejectVerifier), NoPathFound (empty pool). It does NOT cover BudgetExceeded propagation, despite the rustdoc explicitly documenting that variant (lib.rs:934-935: "DepthExceeded / BudgetExceeded — propagated from build_path_candidates when the iterator surfaces them"). Risk: a future refactor of the propagation path (e.g., a well-intentioned contributor folding BudgetExceeded into NoValidPath because "they're both no-path results") will silently change semantics with no test failure. The fixture pattern from tests/integration.rs:test_iterator_budget_bounded_across_calls is reusable — a budget-tight config on a pool that yields one rejected candidate before exhaustion would exercise the propagation. Also missing: DepthExceeded propagation, but that's less critical because the depth-probe logic in build_first_valid_path_with_config (lib.rs:1031-1042) has its own subtle case-split between "zero candidates yielded → probe" and "some candidates yielded but all rejected → NoValidPath wins".
title: no test exercises BudgetExceeded propagation through build_first_valid_path
